summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA)** — kinship-guardianship assistance  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. § 673(d))** — authorizes Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP)

primary_citations.citation_text: Louisiana - Children’s Code Article 601 et seq. (Children’s Code – Child in Need of Care, includes reporting duties)
Louisiana - La. R.S. 46:288.1 et seq. (Extended Foster Care Program Act)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Louisiana Supreme Court held that a Children's Code guardianship may be modified or terminated only under La. Ch.C. art. 724, which requires the mover to prove by clear and convincing evidence a substantial and material change in the circumstances of the guardian or the child, not under the Civil Code best-interest custody standard.
key_cases.relevance: Is the controlling Louisiana authority on the durability of guardianship permanency and what a parent must prove to undo it.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the proper standard for determining whether an order of guardianship should be modified or terminated is statutorily prescribed by Article 724 of the Children's Code

key_cases.court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Second Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court of appeal affirmed the denial of the mother's motion to modify a disposition placing the child with her adult half-brother and affirmed the appointment of the half-brother as guardian, finding no manifest error in the conclusion that guardianship was the most appropriate permanent plan.
key_cases.relevance: Is a worked example of kinship guardianship selected as the permanent plan over a parent's objection.
key_cases.quote: The trial court may modify a judgment of disposition on its own motion or on the motion of the district attorney, the department, the child or his/her parents.

key_cases.court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Second Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court of appeal affirmed the change of the child's permanent plan to adoption after three adjudications, nine placements and nearly five years in foster care, holding the court must select the plan most appropriate and in the child's best interest and that the department had exceeded reasonable efforts at reunification.
key_cases.relevance: Compares guardianship with adoption as competing permanency options and explains why adoption was selected.
key_cases.quote: The court is required to determine the permanent plan for the child that is most appropriate and in the best interest of the child.

extended_foster_care_age: 18 to 21 (voluntary Extended Foster Care Program; must have been adjudicated a child in need of care and in DCFS custody the day before turning 18, plus a school, work, or medical condition; La. R.S. 46:288.2(3), 288.3)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
